extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journalists, policymakers, foundation staff, and members of the public interested in civic information, media trust, free expression, and diversity in asset management
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page describing Knight Foundation's commissioned research priorities and series; summarizes thematic areas and goals (e.g., civic information, free expression, asset-manager diversity, media trust). Useful for understanding what kinds of research the foundation commissions and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to understanding informed and engaged communities
rubrics_metrics.description: We commission research that contributes to the broader understanding of informed and engaged communities, both now and in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the primary purpose for Knight's commissioned research — studies should further knowledge about how communities stay informed and engage civically; projects that do not advance this understanding are outside the stated mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on key thematic areas of significance to the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our commissioned research has focused on key thematic areas that contribute to ongoing conversations of significance to the foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposals and projects are expected to align with Knight Foundation's thematic priorities (examples on the page include Information and Society, Free Expression, Diversity of Asset Managers, Trust/Media/Democracy). Alignment with these topics is implied as a selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pew–Knight Initiative goal: civic information, beliefs, identities, and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew Research Center and Knight Foundation joined forces to launch the Pew–Knight Initiative, an effort to deepen our understanding of how Americans absorb civic information, form beliefs and identities, and engage in their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research under this initiative should address information uptake, belief formation, identity, and civic engagement dynamics among Americans; methodological emphasis and topical fit with these sub-questions are implied priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research on free expression / First Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight Free Expression Research Series — Knight Foundation values the First Amendment, evident in our ongoing research on free expression since 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that examine aspects of free expression, speech on campuses, book restrictions, and First Amendment trends over time are highlighted. Longitudinal or policy-relevant studies on free expression are consistent with this series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and diversity in asset management
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight Diversity of Asset Managers Research Series — since 2017, we have published research to foster transparency about the use of diverse owned asset managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research that documents, measures, or promotes transparency and diversity practices in asset management (e.g., higher education endowments) aligns with this criterion; applied or evaluative work that informs foundation investment practice is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of media trust, news sustainability, and internet/technology attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust, Media and Democracy — from 2017 to 2022 Knight Foundation and Gallup studied media trust, news sustainability, and attitudes towards internet policy and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies that explore public trust in media, business models and sustainability of news, and public attitudes toward internet policy and technology fit within this theme; measuring trends, producing reports, and producing media-impactable findings are emphasized by past work.
